items.prompt: Which question is a valid statistical investigative question?
choices: What proportion of students at the school walk or bike to school?
Did Maya walk to school today?
What is the school mascot?
Is walking better than driving for every student?
items.rationale: A statistical investigative question anticipates variability and identifies a population or sample from which data can be collected.
choiceRationales: Best answer. A statistical investigative question anticipates variability and identifies a population or sample from which data can be collected.
This asks about one person on one day, so there is no variability to investigate and no population to describe.
The mascot is a single fact with one answer, not a question whose answers vary across a group.
This is an opinion question about every student, not a measurable characteristic that varies and can be estimated from data.

items.prompt: In a survey of 240 students, 84 choose the later lunch period. What is the relative frequency for that category?
items.rationale: Relative frequency is the category count divided by the total count: 84/240 = 0.35.
choiceRationales: 0.28 would be 84 out of 300; the survey had 240 students, so the relative frequency is 84/240 = 0.35.
0.65 is 1 − 0.35, the share of students who did not choose the later period, not the share who did.
Best answer. Relative frequency is the category count divided by the total count: 84/240 = 0.35.
2.86 comes from dividing the total by the category count (240/84); relative frequency divides the other way and must be at most 1.

items.prompt: A histogram of commute times has most observations between 10 and 25 minutes and a long right tail. How should the distribution be described?
choices: Unimodal and skewed right
Uniform and symmetric
Bimodal and skewed left
Unimodal and exactly normal
items.rationale: The concentration near smaller values with a longer tail toward larger values indicates right skewness; the single main peak is unimodal.
choiceRationales: Best answer. The concentration near smaller values with a longer tail toward larger values indicates right skewness; the single main peak is unimodal.
A uniform shape has no peak and equal heights; this histogram has a clear concentration between 10 and 25 minutes and a long tail.
There is one main peak, not two, and a long right tail means the skew is to the right.
A normal shape is symmetric; a long right tail rules out normality even though the distribution has one peak.

items.prompt: Which statistic is generally most resistant to an unusually large outlier in a quantitative distribution?
choices: The mean
The median
The standard deviation
The range
items.rationale: The median and IQR are resistant summaries; a very large value can pull the mean and increase the range and standard deviation.
choiceRationales: The mean adds every value, so one very large observation pulls it upward; it is not resistant.
Best answer. The median and IQR are resistant summaries; a very large value can pull the mean and increase the range and standard deviation.
Standard deviation squares each distance from the mean, so a single extreme value inflates it substantially.
The range is the maximum minus the minimum, so an unusually large value changes it directly.

items.prompt: A distribution has mean 52 and standard deviation 6. What is the z-score for an observation of 64?
items.rationale: The z-score is (64 − 52)/6 = 2, so the observation is two standard deviations above the mean.
choiceRationales: A negative z-score would mean the observation is below the mean; 64 is above 52, so the sign is positive.
0.5 is the standard deviation divided by the distance (6/12); the z-score divides the distance by the standard deviation, 12/6 = 2.
Best answer. The z-score is (64 − 52)/6 = 2, so the observation is two standard deviations above the mean.
12 is the raw distance from the mean (64 − 52) before dividing by the standard deviation of 6.

items.prompt: A boxplot has minimum 4, first quartile 9, median 13, third quartile 18, and maximum 27. What is the interquartile range?
items.rationale: The IQR is Q3 − Q1 = 18 − 9 = 9.
choiceRationales: 5 is Q1 minus the minimum (9 − 4), which describes the lower whisker, not the middle half.
14 is the third quartile minus the minimum (18 − 4); the IQR uses Q3 minus Q1.
23 is the range (27 − 4), which measures the full spread, not the spread of the middle 50%.
Best answer. The IQR is Q3 − Q1 = 18 − 9 = 9.

items.prompt: Two classes have the same median test score. Class A has a smaller IQR than Class B. What does that indicate?
choices: The middle 50% of Class A scores are less spread out.
Class A must have the larger mean.
Class A has more scores below its median.
Class B must have a higher maximum score.
items.rationale: The IQR measures the spread of the middle half of a distribution; it does not determine the mean or the extremes.
choiceRationales: Best answer. The IQR measures the spread of the middle half of a distribution; it does not determine the mean or the extremes.
The IQR measures spread of the middle half and says nothing about the mean; equal medians with different IQRs are consistent with any ordering of means.
By definition about half of each class is below its own median; the IQR does not change that.
A larger IQR means a wider middle half, but the maximum is an extreme value the IQR does not determine.

items.prompt: A researcher changes the wording of a survey question after seeing that the first wording produced an unexpected result. Why is that a problem?
choices: It guarantees a larger random sample.
Changing the question after seeing results can make the study question depend on the observed data.
It turns an observational study into a randomized experiment.
It eliminates all response bias.
items.rationale: A valid investigative question should be determined before the analysis so the study is not retrofitted to a desired or surprising result.
choiceRationales: Rewording a question changes nothing about how many people are sampled or how they were selected.
Best answer. A valid investigative question should be determined before the analysis so the study is not retrofitted to a desired or surprising result.
An experiment requires imposing treatments with random assignment; changing survey wording does not do that.
Wording chosen to chase a result is more likely to introduce response bias than to remove it.

items.prompt: Why is random assignment used in an experiment?
choices: It guarantees that every participant receives the preferred treatment.
It allows the researcher to generalize to every population.
It tends to balance lurking variables across treatment groups.
It prevents the response variable from varying.
items.rationale: Random assignment reduces systematic differences among treatment groups and supports cause-and-effect conclusions.
choiceRationales: Random assignment deliberately gives participants no choice of treatment; that is how it balances groups.
Generalization depends on how participants were sampled, not on how they were assigned to treatments.
Best answer. Random assignment reduces systematic differences among treatment groups and supports cause-and-effect conclusions.
The response still varies; random assignment makes group differences attributable to treatment rather than lurking variables.

items.prompt: If all response values are multiplied by 3, what happens to the correlation with the explanatory variable?

It remains the same if the multiplier is positive.

It changes sign.
items.rationale: Correlation is unchanged by positive linear rescaling of either variable.
choiceRationales: Correlation is unitless and unaffected by multiplying a variable by a positive constant.
Best answer. Correlation is unchanged by positive linear rescaling of either variable.
Rescaling preserves the linear relationship, so the correlation keeps its value.
A positive multiplier preserves direction; only a negative multiplier would flip the sign.

items.prompt: A regression slope is 1.8 response units per explanatory unit. What is the predicted change for a 5-unit increase in x?
choices: 1.8 response units.
3.2 response units.
9 response units.
90 response units.
items.rationale: The predicted change is slope times change in x: 1.8(5) = 9.
choiceRationales: 1.8 is the change for a one-unit increase; a five-unit increase multiplies it by 5.
3.2 does not come from the slope; the predicted change is slope times change in x.
Best answer. The predicted change is slope times change in x: 1.8(5) = 9.
90 multiplies by 50 instead of 5.

items.learningObjectiveLabel: Linear Regression Models

items.prompt: A regression line has intercept 6. What does the intercept represent?
choices: The correlation coefficient.
The residual for every observation.
The predicted response at the sample mean only.
The predicted response when the explanatory variable equals zero, if that value is meaningful in context.
items.rationale: The intercept is the model prediction at x = 0, but interpretation requires x = 0 to be meaningful and within scope.
choiceRationales: The intercept is a model coefficient in response units, not the unitless correlation.
Residuals vary by point and are computed from observed minus predicted values.
The intercept is the prediction at x = 0; the prediction at the mean of x is the mean of y.
Best answer. The intercept is the model prediction at x = 0, but interpretation requires x = 0 to be meaningful and within scope.

items.prompt: A residual plot fans outward as x increases. What condition may be violated?
choices: Constant variance of the residuals.
The response must be categorical.
The correlation must equal zero.
The sample must be a census.
items.rationale: A funnel shape suggests that the spread of residuals changes across x.
choiceRationales: Best answer. A funnel shape suggests that the spread of residuals changes across x.
Residual plots require a quantitative response; a fan shape concerns changing spread, not variable type.
A fan pattern in residuals says nothing about the correlation being zero.
Residual plots do not depend on how the sample was drawn; the funnel indicates non-constant variance.

items.learningObjectiveLabel: Interpreting Linear Regression Models

items.prompt: A model has r-squared = 0.49. Which statement is appropriate?
choices: The correlation must be 0.49 regardless of direction.
The linear model explains about 49% of the observed variation in the response.
The model is correct for 49% of individuals.
There is a 49% chance of causation.
items.rationale: R-squared is the proportion of response variation explained by the fitted linear model, not a probability or accuracy rate.
choiceRationales: The correlation magnitude is the square root of 0.49, which is 0.70, with a sign given by the direction.
Best answer. R-squared is the proportion of response variation explained by the fitted linear model, not a probability or accuracy rate.
r-squared is a share of variation explained, not a count of individuals predicted correctly.
r-squared measures fit; it says nothing about causation.

items.learningObjectiveLabel: Least-Squares Regression

items.prompt: Why does a least-squares line use squared residuals?
choices: Squaring makes every residual positive before fitting.
It forces the line through every point.
Squaring prevents positive and negative residuals from canceling.
It removes the need to inspect the scatterplot.
items.rationale: The squared residual criterion measures total error without cancellation and defines the least-squares fit.
choiceRationales: The purpose is to prevent cancellation in the sum, not merely to change signs; positive and negative residuals still exist after fitting.
No line passes through every point of scattered data; least squares minimizes the total squared error.
Best answer. The squared residual criterion measures total error without cancellation and defines the least-squares fit.
The plot should always be examined; the squaring criterion does not check whether a line is appropriate.

items.prompt: A regression model is used to predict a response for an x-value just beyond the observed range. What should be stated?
choices: The prediction is guaranteed accurate because it is close.
The response must be zero.
The model proves a causal effect.
The prediction is a mild extrapolation and should be treated cautiously.
items.rationale: Any prediction outside the observed range is extrapolation, even if the distance beyond the range is small.
choiceRationales: Even a small extrapolation assumes the pattern continues beyond the data, which is not guaranteed.
Nothing about extrapolation forces the predicted response to zero.
Regression predictions do not establish causation regardless of where they are made.
Best answer. Any prediction outside the observed range is extrapolation, even if the distance beyond the range is small.
